title: Mock Test

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
Vishnu and Vignesh are always like two peas in a pod.
questions.solution: A)Like two peas in a pod(idiom) – Very similar to each other बहुत समान

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.
Independence Day is considered as a red-letter day in the history of India.
questions.solution: C)Red-letter day(idiom) – Memorable day यादगार दिन

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
Prakash could not make up his mind about what to do with the project.
questions.solution: A)Make up his mind(idiom) – Decide निर्णय लेना

questions.question:
Choose the option that best describes the meaning of the idioms and phrases underlined in the given sentence.
You can best identify the fair weather friends at the time of adversity.
options: Friend only at the time of prosperity
Friends who come in good weather conditions
questions.solution: C)Fair weather friends(idiom) – Friend only at the time of prosperity केवल समृद्धि के समय का मित्र

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.
I can’t begin to talk on this situation right now; I am still wrapping my head around it.
options: Comparing two things that can’t be compared
questions.solution: D)Wrapping my head around it(idiom) – Understanding something complicated जटिल चीज को समझना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Walk a tightrope
options: To walk on a narrow road
To act carefully in a difficult situation
questions.solution: C)Walk a tightrope (idiom) – To act carefully in a difficult situationमुश्किल स्थिति में सावधानी से कार्य करना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
A bolt from the blue
options: Thunder and rain in a strom
questions.solution: A)A bolt from the blue(idiom) – A sudden and unexpected event अचानक और अप्रत्याशित घटना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To cost an arm and a leg
options: Someone does not have money to buy something
questions.solution: D)To cost an arm and a leg(idiom) – Something is very expensive बहुत महंगा

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To be at daggers drawn
questions.solution: A) To be at daggers drawn(idiom) – Ready to fight लड़ाई के लिए तैयार होना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Bag and baggage
questions.solution: A)Bag and baggage(idiom) – With all goods पूरा सामान

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
The United Nations is working to eliminate the vicious cycle of poverty
questions.solution: D)The vicious cycle(idiom) – One problem causes another एक समस्या दूसरी समस्या का कारण बनती है

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Bread and butter
options: An activity you do to get help others
An activity you do to get money for basic needs
An activity you do to improve your culinary skills
An activity you do with determination
questions.solution: B) Bread and butter (idiom) – An activity you do to get money for basic needsजीवनयापनकासाधन

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiomatic expression that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Last year art critics praised Animesh as if he were a master, but he turned out to be a pleasure for a short time
options: a bull in a china shop
questions.solution: D) a nine days’ wonder(idiom) – a pleasure for a short time थोड़े समय के लिए सुख

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
When I got an opportunity to start a new business, Ravikanth queered my pitch.
options: Helped me by standing beside me
questions.solution: C)Queeredmypitch(idiom) – Ruined my plan योजना बर्बाद करना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Spill the beans
questions.solution: A) Spill the beans(idiom) – To leak a secretराज़ उगल देना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Bells and whistles
options: To take on a difficult task
Attractive but unnecessary features added to products
questions.solution: B)Bells and whistles(idiom) – Attractive but unnecessary features added to products (आकर्षक लेकिन अनावश्यक सुविधाएँ जो उत्पादों में जोड़ी जाती हैं

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Fish out of water
questions.solution: C)Fish out of water(idiom) – To be out of placeअसहज

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Sell like hot cakes
questions.solution: D)Sell like hot cakes (idiom)– Selling out quickly तेज़ी से बिक जाना

questions.question: Which of the following idioms means ‘going to sleep’?
options: Keep an ear to the ground
questions.solution: B)Hit the sack(idiom) – going to sleepसोजाना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Where the shoe pinches
questions.solution: D)Where the shoe pinches(idiom) –Where the difficulty liesकठिनाई होना
